ATK: Attack time: how quickly the envelope rises after a note starts.
DEC: Decay time from the attack peak to the sustain level.
SUS: Sustain level while the key or gate remains held; this is a level, not a time.
REL: Release time after key-up; longer tails continue to consume voices.
PIT: Pitch or pitch modulation depth. In an envelope/LFO destination page this is an amount, not a tuning reference.
PITCH: Pitch or pitch modulation depth. In an envelope/LFO destination page this is an amount, not a tuning reference.
FLT: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
FENV: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
ENV: Filter-envelope amount; positive values open the filter with the envelope, negative values invert that movement where supported.
SHP: Waveform/timbre shaping or the amount of envelope/LFO shaping, according to this page.
SHAPE: Waveform/timbre shaping or the amount of envelope/LFO shaping, according to this page.
RATE: Speed of the selected oscillator/modulator/effect. The displayed unit identifies Hz or a tempo division.
WAVE: Select the oscillator or modulation waveform. Changing the shape changes its harmonic content or movement.
WAVE2: Select the oscillator or modulation waveform. Changing the shape changes its harmonic content or movement.
FADE: Time for LFO modulation to fade in after a note starts.
AMP: Amplitude modulation depth. Start with a small amount to avoid large level swings.
VEL>F: Velocity-to-filter sensitivity; stronger key strikes change brightness.
MW>: Destination controlled by the MIDI modulation wheel.
AT>: Destination controlled by MIDI channel pressure/aftertouch.
SRC: Modulation source for the selected matrix slot.
DST: Modulation destination for the selected matrix slot; engine targets follow the current engine.
AMT: Depth of the selected modulation connection or processor. Bipolar ranges reverse the effect below zero.
SLOT: Select the item being edited; on PROGRAM this is the saved program slot, on MATRIX it is one of the 12 modulation connections.
LANE: Select one of four modulation sequencer lanes.
STEP: Choose the modulation-sequencer step to edit.
VALUE: Set the selected step value, or the exact MIDI CC value required by a pedal assignment.
LEN: Length of the current sequence or setlist. Shorter lengths wrap sooner; a setlist length of zero disables the list.
LENGTH: Length of the current sequence or setlist. Shorter lengths wrap sooner; a setlist length of zero disables the list.
SMTH: Smooth transitions between modulation-sequencer step values.
SYNC: Clock/synchronization source. External sync requires a running clock on the selected input.
CHOR: Chorus amount/send; adds detuned movement and width.
CHO: Chorus amount/send; adds detuned movement and width.
FILT: Part or master DJ-style filter: negative is low-pass, zero OFF, positive high-pass.
INSRT: Select the per-part insert processor; its three following controls change with the type.
INS A: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
INS B: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
INS C: Inactive generic insert parameter when the insert is OFF. Select a processor to reveal its meaningful controls.
MIX: Dry/wet balance or shared effect output level, as identified by the page.
TIME: Delay time. Listen for pitch changes when changing tape-style delay time.
FDBK: Feedback/recirculation. High values prolong the effect and can greatly increase level.
FB: Feedback/recirculation. High values prolong the effect and can greatly increase level.
COLR: Tone or spectral balance of this sound/processor.
TONE: Tone or spectral balance of this sound/processor.
TYPE: Select an effect or MIDI-message type.
DAMP: High-frequency damping; darker reverberation or faster high-frequency decay as raised.
PRE: Reverb pre-delay before the reverberant tail.
LOW: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
MID: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
HIGH: Master EQ gain for the indicated frequency band. Zero dB is neutral.
COMP: Compare the edited CZ tone against its original; use this to judge your edits.
ROOT: Root note of the selected scale. This transposes the scale relationship; it does not transpose every played note.
SCL: Keyboard scale used by note quantization and scale-aware chords.
QNT: OFF leaves note selection chromatic; SNAP moves notes to the chosen scale; WHITE maps white-key playing into that scale. ALL modes apply the setting across all four parts and MIDI input.
CHORD: Chord generator voicing. OFF plays individual notes. Available voicings are filtered for compatibility with the active microtonal scale.
TRN: Transpose this part by semitones; octave shifts are multiples of 12.
TRANS: Transpose this part by semitones; octave shifts are multiples of 12.
STRUM: Spread chord notes in time. The upper values select tempo-synchronized direction/rate combinations.
VCE: POLY plays chords; MONO plays one note; LEG is legato mono; UNI stacks voices. All use the shared budget.
MODEL: Select the filter model exposed by this engine. The capability map determines which controls actually operate.
F1 MODEL: Select the filter model exposed by this engine. The capability map determines which controls actually operate.
CUT: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
F1 CUT: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
LPF: Low-pass/filter cutoff: lower values remove more upper harmonics.
RES: Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation.
F1 RES: Filter resonance emphasizes frequencies around cutoff. High values may change level or approach self-oscillation.
Q: Resonance/sharpness of the vocal formant filters.
DRIVE: Drive into a saturation/filter stage. More drive can add harmonics and change level.
DRV: Drive into a saturation/filter stage. More drive can add harmonics and change level.
TRIM: Sound output calibration in half-dB steps. This changes the sound gain independently of the part mixer level.
VOIC: Chord voicing: CLOSE, SMOOTH, OPEN, INV1, INV2 or +OCT. This changes the layout of generated chord notes, not the part polyphony.
GLMOD: Choose which note transitions use glide.
PRIO: Priority of held notes in a monophonic part.
ALLOC: Voice allocation/unison setting. Extra voices consume the shared eight-voice budget.
DTUNE: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
DTUN: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
DTN: Detuning amount between oscillators/voices or FM operators, according to the selected engine.
VINTG: Vintage variation/drift; adds small imperfections rather than changing the scale.
SPRED: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
SPRD: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
WIDTH: Stereo spread or oscillator/processor width. Check the result in mono.
BPM: Internal tempo in beats per minute.
SWING: Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions.
SWG: Off-beat timing offset. Zero is straight; higher settings delay alternating subdivisions.
TUNE: Select the master tuning system, including maqam and custom/Scala options.
FROM: First octave affected by master tuning, C0-C8. Lower notes remain equal-tempered.
MASTER: Apply master tuning to the selected part; ON by default. OFF bypasses the shared maqam/microtuning for that part.
A4: Reference frequency of A4, in Hz. This is separate from the tuning-system octave boundary.
MIDI: Enable/route sequencer MIDI output according to the listed modes.
IN CH: Accepted MIDI input channel; OMNI accepts all channels, subject to the controller protocol/MPE settings.
OUT: On MIDI: output channel. On FMX ROUTE: selected operator output level.
BEND: Pitch-bend range in semitones; AUTO follows supported configuration messages.
LOCAL: Whether the onboard keyboard drives the internal synth. MIDI input remains a separate path.
EWI: Breath-controller handling: OFF, volume, or volume plus pressure behavior.
KEY IN: Choose USB, TRS or both for keyboard MIDI input.
PORT: MIDI transport/cable selection; AUTO uses automatic controller cable selection where offered.
ACTION: Select the pedal action to learn, edit or test.
LEARN: Arm MIDI learn. Press the pedal once, inspect the captured message, then accept it.
ACCEPT: Commit the captured MIDI message to the selected pedal action.
DUP ms: Duplicate-message suppression window in milliseconds. Zero disables suppression; use the smallest useful window so intentional taps remain distinct.
NUMBER: MIDI CC number or program-change number for this assignment.
CH: MIDI output channel for the MIDI-only track. This track controls external instruments rather than generating audio.
USB ROLE: COMPUTER connects an editor, iPad or computer; PEDAL hosts a class-compliant controller with appropriate powered host hardware. Return to COMPUTER before editing over USB.
SCENE: Choose one of four compact scenes within the working program.
CAPTURE: Store the current supported mix, mutes, sends, macros and tuning settings into the selected scene.
RECALL: Apply the selected captured scene without loading another program.
ENTRY: Choose the position to edit in the ordered setlist.
PROGRAM: Assign a saved program number to this setlist position.
LOAD: Load the selected saved program/setlist entry. Storage actions require their on-screen confirmation.
ON: Enable this part in layered playback.
SPLIT: Enable keyboard-range filtering for this part.
UPPER: OFF uses the lower side, including the boundary. ON uses notes above the boundary.
POINT: Split boundary as a MIDI note number. The held EDIT mixer presents it as a note/octave name.
LEVEL: Level of the selected part/operator/processor; use the page context to identify which one. A zero part level silences that part.
PAN: Position of the selected part in the stereo field; center is zero.
MUTE: Silence the selected part without deleting its sound.
SOLO: Hear the soloed part(s), subject to layer routing/enabled state.
LAYER: Toggle four-part performance. OFF plays the focused part; ON uses enabled parts and their routing.
NAME: Edit the selected saved-program name. ALGORITHM chooses a character position; PRESET/KNOB 2 changes its character.
SAVE: Write the working four-part program to the selected saved slot after confirmation.
CLRSQ: Clear sequence data using the requested confirmation; this is destructive to the working pattern.
INIT: Initialize the selected working sound. Save a copy before using it.
NEW: Initialize the working project/program as requested by the confirmation. Back up wanted edits first.
MODE: Choose the operating mode for this page: LFO restart, arp direction, delay style, controller protocol or operator frequency mode.
OCT: Arpeggiator octave range or part octave shift, depending on the page.
GATE: Duration of each generated arp/sequence note as a fraction of its step.
PROB: Probability of playing a generated note. Lower settings deliberately omit some notes.
HOLD: Keep the arpeggiated/held notes after key-up. Turn off to release the latched note set.
ORD: Order in which held notes enter the arpeggiator.
SPICE: Amount of controlled variation applied to generated notes.
DICE: Variation seed/reroll control. TURNG mode changes its interpretation to a repeating random sequence seed.
LOOP: Repeat/loop behavior. On ENV 2, ONE is a single contour and LOOP repeats it; on SPICE/TURNG it repeats generated variation.
DIV: Pattern step division relative to tempo.
MOD: On MOD PRESET, choose a ready-made expressive routing; other pages use it for modulation amount.
APPLY: Apply the selected modulation template. Existing required slots are checked before changing routings.
OP: Select one of the six FMX operators to edit.
RATIO: Operator frequency ratio relative to the played note.
FINE: Fine operator tuning within the selected ratio.
VEL: Velocity sensitivity of the operator/modulation target.
KSC: Keyboard scaling of the selected operator level.
FREQ: Fixed-versus-ratio frequency behavior for the selected FMX operator.
ALG: FM/operator connection algorithm. Each choice changes which oscillators modulate or reach the output.
BITS: Bit depth of the crusher. Lower settings add quantization distortion.
HPF: High-pass cutoff; reduce unwanted low-frequency energy.
SUB: Sub-oscillator level under the main oscillator.
PW: Pulse width/duty cycle; changes harmonic balance.
DUTY: Pulse width/duty cycle; changes harmonic balance.
OSC2: Second oscillator setting/level. Use the engine description to distinguish oscillator type from mix.
HARM: Harmonic content/structure of the selected model.
POS: Position in a sample, wavetable, wave sequence or excitation, as indicated by the engine.
START: Position in a sample, wavetable, wave sequence or excitation, as indicated by the engine.
TABL: Select the wavetable. USER WT remains silent until a user table is uploaded.
VOWL: Formant/vowel position; moving it changes the vocal resonance.
VOWL2: Formant/vowel position; moving it changes the vocal resonance.
16': Level of the 16' string register. Blend registers to change the ensemble voicing.
8': Level of the 8' string register. Blend registers to change the ensemble voicing.
4': Level of the 4' string register. Blend registers to change the ensemble voicing.
DENS: Grain density; more overlapping grains make a denser texture.
BOW: Bowing/excitation behavior of the physical model.
IDX: FM/phase modulation index; higher values generally add sidebands.
INT2: Pitch interval for the additional oscillator/voice in the trio.
INT3: Pitch interval for the additional oscillator/voice in the trio.
LPG: Low-pass gate behavior of the model.
X: Coordinate in the vector/terrain mix; moving between sources changes the timbre.
Y: Coordinate in the vector/terrain mix; moving between sources changes the timbre.
MRPH: Morph amount between the model waveforms.
SHIFT: Shift the vocal formants without changing the played musical note.
KTR: Keyboard tracking: changes the filter/model response with played pitch.
KTRK: Keyboard tracking: changes the filter/model response with played pitch.
VENV: Envelope amount applied to the VPS phase slope.
M1: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M2: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M3: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
M4: One of four macro controls. HYBRID uses patch-defined macro assignments; other engines provide brightness, timbre, motion and space behavior.
A: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
B: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
C: Model/operator component parameter; its meaning follows the selected engine and model.
D: VPS phase breakpoint; moves the point where the oscillator changes slope.
LINE: Select CZ line combination: one line, both lines, or their supported mixed/modulated configuration.
V: VPS phase slope; changes harmonic content independently of oscillator pitch.
SWP: Sweep amount or rate of the selected engine.
ARP: Engine-specific arpeggiation/model control; the dedicated ARP menu remains the performance arpeggiator.
CPU: Live processor-load display; a diagnostic indication, not a volume control. Persistent overload can cause crackling.
-: Unused control position; turning this knob has no assigned sound parameter on this layout.
--: Unused control position; turning this knob has no assigned sound parameter on this layout.
Unused control; turning it has no action on this screen.
1 > 2: Copy the first CZ synthesis line into the second line. This replaces line 2 settings.
2 > 1: Copy the second CZ synthesis line into the first line. This replaces line 1 settings.
A.KEY: Keyboard scaling of the amplitude envelope: changes envelope response across the keyboard.
W.KEY: Keyboard scaling of the waveform envelope: changes its response across the keyboard.
ABOUT: Turn right to open firmware version, credits and device information. No sound parameter is changed.
ALIAS: Sample-hold rate of the bitcrusher. Lower effective rates introduce aliasing and a rough digital texture.
AMD: Amplitude-modulation depth of the native FM LFO; produces tremolo on operators with AMS enabled.
AMS: Sensitivity of this operator to amplitude modulation from the native FM LFO.
AMT1: Depth of the selected modulation route. Negative values reverse the direction; zero disables its influence.
AT FLT: Enable channel-pressure control of filter cutoff. Press harder on an aftertouch-capable controller to brighten the sound.
AT LFO: Enable channel-pressure control of native LFO depth.
AUDIO CLICK: Metronome behavior: OFF, during REC only, or ON during playback.
AUTOSAVE: Keep automatic working-project saves after playback stops and the instrument is idle. Named program saves remain a separate operation.
BEND+: Maximum upward pitch-bend interval in semitones.
BEND-: Maximum downward pitch-bend interval in semitones.
BITE: Amount of the processor character/distortion; raise gradually while listening for extra harmonics.
BOOT: Choose the project loaded on startup: OFF or A-D. OFF uses the normal startup/template behavior; this is separate from named program slots.
BRK: Keyboard breakpoint separating the left and right operator-level scaling regions.
BUDGET: Shared synthesis allocation budget (8-32 points). All four parts compete for this total; raising it can increase CPU load and crackling.
CALIBRATION: Turn right to enter hardware control calibration. Follow the on-screen prompts; do not enter during a performance.
CENTS: Detune the selected chromatic note from -100 to +100 cents in 10-cent device steps. The editors offer 1-cent steps.
CHORD ENTRY: HOLD replaces the current entered chord while keys are held; ADD accumulates notes for step entry.
CHRD: Chord generation mode. OFF plays single notes; DIA3/DIA7 use scale degrees; fixed shapes and AUTO/AUTO2 provide other harmonies. Microtonal compatibility restricts available choices.
CLICK LEVEL: Metronome loudness: LOW, MID or HIGH.
CLK: Clock source: INT uses the FM-1 tempo; USB or TRS follows incoming MIDI clock on that connection.
COLOR: Choose a saved display palette. Changes the appearance of the device, not synthesis or the editor palette.
COUNT-IN: Recording count-in: OFF, 1 BAR or 2 BARS.
CRS: Coarse frequency of the selected FM operator. Ratio mode follows note pitch; fixed mode uses an absolute frequency range.
CUTOFF: Filter cutoff. Lower settings remove more high-frequency content; resonance emphasizes the cutoff region.
DECAY: Tail/decay length of this effect. Higher values generally keep the effect sounding longer.
DECY: Drum-kit decay amount. Shorten it for tighter hits and fewer overlapping tails.
DEG: Scale degree assigned to pad 02 in MPC quantization mode; establishes the pad-bank layout.
DELAY: Delay before the selected modulation begins; it does not move the played note itself.
DETUNE: Pitch spread between voices or oscillators. Small values add width; large values sound deliberately out of tune.
DST1: Destination of the selected matrix route. Engine destinations E1-E8 follow the active instrument controls.
DXVEL: DX7-style velocity normalization/response option. Changes how incoming velocity reaches the FM engine.
END: Final segment of the CZ envelope. Segments after END are not played.
ENGIN: FM rendering model. This changes the native FM implementation/character rather than selecting a different part.
ENV AMT: Amount of envelope modulation applied to the destination named by this page.
FILTER: Enable the modulation source on filter cutoff.
FINE B: Fine detuning of oscillator B relative to oscillator A.
FOCUS: Spectral focus/character of the selected processor; adjust by ear alongside its mix.
FONT: Choose RUBIK or PIXEL for the device text.
FREQ A: Oscillator A pitch. In a modulation-routing page this is an on/off destination switch instead.
FREQ B: Oscillator B pitch. In a modulation-routing page this is an on/off destination switch instead.
FX: Select the shared audio effect in the highlighted rack row.
NOTE FX: Select note processing for the highlighted part-rack row: OFF, NOTE TAIL or NOTE ECHO.
GLIDE: Pitch-slide time between notes; most noticeable in mono/legato playing.
GLISS: Quantize portamento into discrete semitone steps instead of a continuous slide.
GUARD: Enable overload protection that can cut voices to protect the audio deadline. It is not output loudness compensation.
INITIAL: Native LFO depth before any modulation-wheel input.
JITTER: Random variation introduced by the processor; raise for a less stable texture.
KEY: Choose a chromatic key for tuning, or keyboard-tracking mode on a filter page, as identified above.
KEY B: Make oscillator B follow played keyboard pitch. OFF allows B to remain an independent modulation source.
KIT: Drum sample/kit selection. This changes the sound sources for the drum lanes.
KNOB ACCEL: ON makes faster turns cover larger value changes; OFF gives more consistent small adjustments.
KSYNC: Restart native FM LFO phase on each note when enabled; OFF allows free-running phase.
LCRV: Operator-level scaling curve below the breakpoint: linear or exponential, rising or falling.
RCRV: Operator-level scaling curve above the breakpoint: linear or exponential, rising or falling.
LDEP: Depth of operator-level scaling below the breakpoint.
RDEP: Depth of operator-level scaling above the breakpoint.
LIGHTS: Choose the behavior of keyboard/button illumination. This does not change note velocity.
LOW B: Switch oscillator B into its low-frequency range for modulation.
MIXA: Performance offset to oscillator A level; the native patch mixer remains the underlying setting.
MIXB: Performance offset to oscillator B level; the native patch mixer remains the underlying setting.
N MIX: Mix noise into wheel modulation. Low settings favor the native LFO; high settings favor noise.
NOTE: Semitone detune component for the CZ line combination.
NOTE PREVIEW: Play an audible preview when selecting/editing sequence notes. OFF is useful for silent editing.
OSC A: Oscillator A level in the synthesis mixer.
OSC B: Oscillator B level in the mixer, or its modulation-source amount on POLYMOD.
PART: Apply master tuning to the selected part. ON follows the global scale; OFF bypasses it for this part.
PICKER POPUPS: Enable automatic value pickers while editing enumerated choices.
PMS: Pitch-modulation sensitivity of the native FM voice.
POL: BI moves modulation above and below center; UNI moves in one direction from zero.
PORTA: Native FM portamento time between pitches.
PRIORITY: Native unison/retrigger note-priority behavior. Determines which held key drives the voice.
RELEASE: Enable the Prophet release stages after key-up. When OFF, release controls do not produce the expected tails.
RESO: Resonance/feedback intensity in the selected modulation effect.
ROUT: CH1-4/CH5-8/CH9-12/CH13-16 route consecutive MIDI channels to the parts. SEL routes input to the focused part.
ROUTE: CHAIN feeds the shared processors in sequence. SPLIT uses the separate part sends to the shared effect slots.
RSCL: Keyboard rate scaling: changes FM envelope speed with played pitch.
SCALE: Select the master scale. W/, A/ and T/ abbreviate Western, Arabic and Turkish names on the device.
SCREEN OFF: Display sleep timeout: NEVER, 5, 15, 30 or 60 minutes. The audio engine continues operating.
SIGN: Direction of CZ detuning: positive or negative.
SNAP: Enable master scale quantization for all four parts and MIDI, subject to tuning application settings.
SPEED: Rate of the native FM LFO.
SRC1: Source of the selected modulation route: LFO, envelope, velocity, key tracking, random or a MIDI controller.
STACK: SID oscillator/voice stacking configuration; changes the combined waveform character and voice load.
STORE: Write the native voice into the chosen USER sound slot after confirmation. Stop playback before saving.
STROKE: Strum direction: DOWN, UP or ALT (alternating).
TRIG: NOTE restarts the LFO for each note; FREE keeps it running independently.
TRNS: Transpose the native FM voice in semitones.
TRS: Enable MIDI output on the TRS connection for this MIDI-only track.
TUNA: Performance tuning offset for oscillator A.
TUNB: Performance tuning offset for oscillator B.
UNISON: Stack voices on the same note. This uses additional points from the shared voice budget.
USB AUDIO: IN+OUT, IN, OUT or OFF enables the corresponding USB audio directions.
USB INPUT: Choose stereo master input or four-track audio input routing. Requires COMPUTER USB role.
USE: Enable or bypass the global tuning system.
V.AMP: Velocity sensitivity of the CZ amplitude envelope.
V.PIT: Velocity sensitivity of the CZ pitch envelope.
V.WAV: Velocity sensitivity of the CZ waveform envelope.
VEL AMP: Enable note velocity modulation of the Prophet amplifier envelope.
VEL FLT: Enable note velocity modulation of the Prophet filter envelope.
VINTAGE: Analog-style variation between voices. Adds instability/character rather than a fixed tuning shift.
VOICES: Native Prophet unison voice count; actual allocation is still limited by the shared budget.
SAW A: Enable the saw a waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
SAW B: Enable the saw b waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
TRI B: Enable the tri b waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
PULSE A: Enable the pulse a waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
PULSE B: Enable the pulse b waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
SAW: Enable the saw waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
TRI: Enable the tri waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
SQUARE: Enable the square waveform. Multiple enabled waveforms are combined.
PW A: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
PW B: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
PWA: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
PWB: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
WIDTH A: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
WIDTH B: Pulse width of the named oscillator; changes its harmonic balance. On a routing page, enables modulation of that pulse width.
P5: Allocation cost per sounding P5 voice. AUTO uses the built-in cost; a numbered override changes how quickly this engine consumes the shared budget.
CZ-1: Allocation cost per sounding CZ-1 voice. AUTO uses the built-in cost; a numbered override changes how quickly this engine consumes the shared budget.
FM6: Allocation cost per sounding FM6 voice. AUTO uses the built-in cost; a numbered override changes how quickly this engine consumes the shared budget.
SID: Allocation cost per sounding SID voice. AUTO uses the built-in cost; a numbered override changes how quickly this engine consumes the shared budget.
KICK: Level of the kick drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
SNARE: Level of the snare drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
CLAP: Level of the clap drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
HATCL: Level of the hatcl drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
HATOP: Level of the hatop drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
TOM: Level of the tom drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
RIM: Level of the rim drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
BELL: Level of the bell drum lane; reduce to balance that instrument against the kit.
WHEEL: Response range/depth for the wheel MIDI performance controller.
FOOT: Response range/depth for the foot MIDI performance controller.
BREATH: Response range/depth for the breath MIDI performance controller.
AFTER: Response range/depth for the after MIDI performance controller.
W.DST: Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice.
F.DST: Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice.
B.DST: Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice.
A.DST: Destination combination for this controller: pitch, amplitude and/or envelope bias, according to the displayed choice.
VOL1: Volume of part 1. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses.
VOL2: Volume of part 2. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses.
VOL3: Volume of part 3. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses.
VOL4: Volume of part 4. This is independent of which part SELECT currently focuses.
